correctness.rationale: Exact Beta-prime density of the squared block norms is derived from Haar invariance; both integrals converge for all finite positive parameters. Moving-boundary differentiation cancels exactly. The derivative has the sign of pJ_+−qJ_−. Its ratio has a strict monotonic logarithmic derivative because its two probability kernels have disjoint ordered supports. Explicit endpoints put q/p strictly between the ratio limits for t≠n and reverse the derivative sign across one root; this proves uniqueness and global optimality analytically. The n-th moment equals volume divided by unit-ball volume, while the n+2 isotropic formula follows by elementary factorwise second-moment integration. The included standalone numerical checker passed; no infinite inference relies on its finite samples.

value.rationale: This resolves a natural one-parameter geometric optimization family that joins mean central chord lengths to dual-quermassintegrals. The structural theorem gives every real positive moment, all factor dimensions, a sharp transition precisely at ambient dimension, strict global optimizer uniqueness and computable integral equations in the subcritical regime where the older general theory gives necessary conditions but not universal sufficiency. The family is not an arbitrary numerical slice: all fixed-volume orthogonal two-ball products occur, with the isotropic second-moment position as a natural calibration.
